first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ—a direct signal that something in the funnel has degraded. Memory_86 and memory_31 both showed that lightweight onboarding changes (shortening flows, cutting fields) improved activation and time-to-value for self-serve SMB segments with durable effect. The competitive pricing pressure makes time-to-value especially valuable: faster activated accounts are less likely to churn to cheaper alternatives. A simplified onboarding intervention is low-risk, directly addresses an observed metric decline, and has proven precedent. Verification of those two memories will confirm the magnitude of prior lift and whether conditions have changed. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers but don't help new acquisitions against competitor pricing. Promotional pricing (memory_73) risks margin erosion in an already competitive moment and is reactive. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a secondary lever—engagement gains follow only after accounts complete onboarding. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) addresses a different segment and doesn't solve SMB activation loss. Given one experiment slot and the need to maximize sustainable qualified revenue, stopping the activation decline via onboarding simplification is the highest-leverage move.
